q: Roughly what does climbing two flights of stairs without stopping represent?
why: Two flights without stopping is the usual practical marker of at least 4 METs; under 4 METs suggests higher perioperative risk.

q: When should an SGLT2 inhibitor usually be stopped before elective surgery?
o: The day before and the day of surgery
why: Current UK guidance is to omit SGLT2 inhibitors the day before and the day of surgery, because of the risk of euglycaemic DKA, and check ketones.

q: Above what HbA1c is elective surgery usually deferred?
why: Elective surgery is usually deferred if HbA1c is above 69 mmol/mol (8.5%), unless the benefit of surgery outweighs the risk.
